name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.32.0 — every review ledger row now names the code it judged (specs/20260824/06-review-range-identity.md): `spec-review-driver.js` resolves its base ref (`build_base → diff_base → merge-base`) to a full sha once via `git rev-parse --verify <base>^{commit}` — a base that fails to resolve is now a `die` naming the `diff_base` remedy, replacing the former warn-and-continue — and re-reads `HEAD` fresh at every verdict pass (hard-stop, escalate, close), passing `--base-sha`/`--head-sha`/`--dirty` (set when `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` is non-empty) to all three. `verdict.js` gains those three flags on the review profile only, refused together, refused on `--profile release`, and refused unless both `--base-sha` and `--head-sha` are a full 40-hex commit sha: the printed row's `diff` object carries `base`/`head`/`dirty` after `loc` in fixed key order, and the retained artifact gains the same object verbatim; `dirty: true` marks a close row whose true upper bound is the close commit that follows it, since fix-worker edits may still be uncommitted at pass time. `review-legs.js`'s reconcile leg now emits its out-of-plan paths beside the count (`{"outOfPlan":N,"files":[…]}`, verbatim from `scope-reconcile.js`, capped at 40 with `filesOmitted` when the cap bites); `countLegFinding` still reads the count, never the array length. Historical rows and retained artifacts are never rewritten; `/spec:escape` step 3 reads the range fields when a correlated row carries them and proceeds exactly as before on older rows. No waive cap exists by ruling — CLEAN stays derivable at any user-adjudicated waive count. 7.31.0 — the render gate lands: mock↔component fidelity is judged at the render, not at the pixel (ADR-0002, specs/20260824/01). Three new scripts, all dependency-free: `render-inventory.browser.js` is a bare in-page expression the host's capture command evaluates, returning an accessibility-tree-shaped inventory of **painted** text (computed `text-transform` applied — DOM text differs from paint on correct code), `aria-label` kept as a separate `name` facet so a label glyph never collides with a real control, roles, page-coordinate boxes, and the `srOnly`/`fixed`/`outOfFlow`/`dataPositioned` flags; `render-compare.js` matches two inventories by LCS over in-flow painted text and reports `text-missing`/`text-extra`/`order`/`role`/`positioning`/`geometry` findings under script-constant tolerances (dx 1%, dw 1%, dh 15% — the measured zero-false-positive floors), with `dyRel` computed into `--json` but never a finding (unbound-region height poisons it) and static-control→link auto-excused behind one printed `📌 Auto-picked` veto line; `render-gate.js` drives the host's declared `design.render.capture` command across the `design/targets.json` theme × viewport matrix, serving the host's `design/` directory itself over Node's built-in `http` on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port so mock-relative `../tokens.css` resolves, binding each mock state to a story id through `.claude/design-coverage.json` claims (`stories`), and honouring a `ready`/`boot` lifecycle that kills only the process it started. Exclusions are structural, never tolerances: `aria-hidden`/`data-contract="none"` subtrees never enter the inventory, absolutely-positioned entries are matched by presence but excluded from ORDER, and fixed/sticky, sr-only, or `data-positioned` entries are excluded from GEOMETRY — each one a measured false-positive class. Exit alphabet 0 pass / 1 findings / 2 precondition / 3 capture-or-readiness failure, so a capture failure can never read as green. No pixel layer exists and the capture contract deliberately has no screenshot output, so no host can wire one back in as a "quick advisory". `spec.config.json` gains the `design.render` block (`capture`, `url`, optional `ready`, `boot`, `readyTimeout`) — a grounding-contract change, so every host's `/spec:doctor` will report stale grounding until it declares the key or refreshes. `/spec:review` runs the gate as an advisory evidence leg on designed specs where `design.render` is declared, and prints one skip line naming the key where it is not; it is never a `verdict.js` leg. 7.30.0 — replay attributes red legs against the originating review's own recorded baseline instead of treating every red leg as mutation evidence, closing a censoring/false-due-window-reset defect measured 2026-08-23 on ~27% of selectable CLEAN closes (specs/20260823/09): `--select` derives the baseline from the selected row's own `legs` array (red = `exit !== 0`, `smoke` exit 4 exempt) with zero extra leg runs, appending `baselineRed=<legs>|none|unknown` and `baselineLegs=<legs>|unknown` after the existing five selection tokens; `spec-review-driver.js`'s `parseSelection` captures both when present (absent → `null`, never a parse failure) and prints them in the REPLAY step body. replay.md's Phase 1 step 7 re-keys the retry/leg-caught path to newly-red legs only: a red leg is explained when it's in `baselineRed` or is `reconcile` (deterministic exemption — the mutation is File-Plan-confined by step 4's worker contract, so reconcile redness, definitionally out-of-plan, can never be mutation-caused); an unattributable red leg routes to one `AskUserQuestion` whose dismissal records `unresolved`. `--record --legs` gains `baseline-red:<leg>[,<leg>]`, valid for `caught`/`missed`/`unresolved` alongside `green`; `unresolved` also keeps a `red:<leg>` arm for a step-7 dismissal, which requires `--patch` and now refuses `--workflow` (the reviewer never ran); `leg-caught` keeps `red:<leg>` for newly-red-only. Historical ledger rows, including the motivating `rp_1b176ebff5c7` misrecord, are never rewritten; `--stats` is unchanged. Deviation: D8 named 7.29.0 as the bump target, but that version was already at HEAD by build time (a concurrent session in this repo won the race) — per this repo's own next-free-version Gotcha this lands at 7.30.0 instead, recorded in the spec's deviations sidecar.
